articles.title: 'Play with the ball that you've got': Tom Latham pushes back on Shubman Gill's concerns over ball quality
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Tom Latham believes the condition of a cricket ball is influenced by the nature of the pitch, whether it is a Dukes or Kookaburra, but
articles.body: New Zealand captain Tom Latham believes the condition of a cricket ball is influenced by the nature of the pitch, whether it is a Dukes or Kookaburra, but said players must learn to adapt rather than look for excuses.Latham's comments came after India captain Shubman Gill raised concerns over the quality of cricket balls following the drawn first Test in Wellington. Gill had said that both Dukes and Kookaburra balls tend to become soft after the first 25-30 overs, affecting their effectiveness.Speaking ahead of the second Test against India, Latham said the surface can play a role in how quickly the ball wears out and teams need to find ways to keep it in good condition."I think sometimes the wicket can dictate what the ball does, whether it's a little bit flatter or a little bit more abrasive, then the ball can deteriorate a little bit quicker, whether that be a Dukes ball, whether that be a Kookaburra ball," Latham said on the eve of the second Test against India."So I think from our point of view, we're always trying to adapt and find what's the best way to look after the ball to keep it in good condition as much as we can."Latham expects the ball to retain its condition for longer at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, given the nature of the surface and the limited cricket played at the venue recently."I think we'll probably see here (Christchurch) throughout the game that it will probably stay newer for longer because of the green surfaces."And there hasn't been a lot of cricket played out here at Hagley, so there's not a lot of used wickets that can deteriorate the ball quicker," he said.The New Zealand skipper also pointed out that the condition of cricket balls can vary between series and seasons, but said players have to work with what they are given."So, I guess it's a series-by-series thing. Sometimes it's a year-by-year thing. Sometimes the balls can be really good. Sometimes maybe not so good, where they deteriorate a little bit more."But we know as cricketers, you've got to be able to play with the ball that you've got. And whether it's in good condition, whether it's not so good, you've got to find a way," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ILT20: Dubai Capitals beat Desert Vipers by 45 runs, register first win of season 5
articles.summary: Dubai Capitals defeated Desert Vipers by 45 runs at the Dubai International Stadium on Wednesday to register their first win of ILT20 season 5.
articles.body: Dubai Capitals defeated Desert Vipers by 45 runs at the Dubai International Stadium on Wednesday to register their first win of ILT20 season 5.Sam Billings' 43 off 31 balls and Rovman Powell's rapid 28 off 12 powered the Capitals to 164/7, before the bowlers took over. Noor Ahmad's four for 20 and Mustafizur Rahman's two for 12 led the way, with Dushmantha Chameera (2/27) and Hassan Khan (2/16) also taking two wickets each as the Vipers were bowled out for 119 in 17.5 overs. Andries Gous's 27 off 30 was the Vipers' top score.Put in to bat first, Dubai Capitals suffered an early blow when Masood Gurbaz (2 off 2) was run out after a mix-up with Faf du Plessis (24 off 30) to leave them at 8/1. Max Holden (22 off 17) joined du Plessis and steered the innings through the powerplay, with a stand of 37 runs in 34 balls.The partnership didn't last as Vipers skipper Shadab Khan had Max Holden caught in the seventh. Soon after, du Plessis, was stumped off Nangeyalia Khan in search of his first boundary of the innings.The Capitals were 61/3 in 9.4 overs when Sam Billings (43 off 31) and Marcus Stoinis (27 off 24) came together for a key stand of 59 runs in 40 balls. With boundaries hard to come by, Billings broke the shackles in the 16th to smash Shadab for a six and two fours.Just as the Capitals looked set for a big finish, Khuzaima Tanveer removed Stoinis to leave the score at 120/4 in 16.2 overs. He then scalped Billings and Karim Janat (6 off 4) in the 19th over to emerge as the pick of the Vipers attack and take over the White Belt (awarded to the best bowler) with eight wickets in three innings.Rovman Powell (28 off 12) provided the finishing touch with a rapid-fire knock, smashing two fours and two sixes including 16 in the final over to catapult the Capitals to 164/7 in 20 overs.In response, the Vipers lost Babar Azam (1 off 2) in the second over off Dushmantha Chameera's bowling to leave them at 2/1. Fakhar Zaman (12 off 11) and Andries Gous added 35 before Fakhar was caught off Mustafizur Rahman in the fifth over, making it 37/2.Noor Ahmad then took charge, removing Joe Clarke (3 off 5) in the seventh and Gous (27 off 30) in the ninth over to leave the Vipers on 48/4.Shimron Hetmyer (19 off 13) and Shadab (16 off 11) tried to rebuild with a 31-run stand, but Chameera ended it by having the Vipers skipper caught in the 12th over. Noor had Hetmyer stumped in the 13th, leaving the Vipers at 83/6.Tom Curran (18 off 8) briefly raised hopes with two fours and a six, but he was caught off Noor for his fourth wicket in the 15th over to make it 102/7.Hassan Khan then struck twice in the 17th with the wickets of Khuzaima Tanveer (9 off 7) and Nangeyalia Khan (6 off 12). Mustafizur returned to dismiss Mujeeb Ur Rahman (2 off 4) as the Vipers were bowled out for 119 in 17.5 overs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'You have to make the new ball count': India coach challenges pacers to do more with the new Kookaburra ahead of must-win Test
articles.summary: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has urged the fast bowlers to make the most of the new Kookaburra ball, saying they need to be willing to take risks, as
articles.body: India bowling coach Morne Morkel has urged the fast bowlers to make the most of the new Kookaburra ball, saying they need to be willing to take risks, as India prepare for the must-win Test in Christchurch to keep their WTC final hopes alive."You have to make the new ball count. You need to be brave sometimes," Morkel said on the eve of the second and final Test against New Zealand in Christchurch.Morkel also backed Anshul Kamboj, who faced questions over his pace during the opening Test in Wellington. Kamboj bowled 45 overs across the two innings, but his speed dropped below 130 kmph during his second and third spells as India struggled to find breakthroughs on a surface that lost pace early.Morkel said it was unfair to single out the Haryana pacer, who had helped India maintain control through his bowling."Anshul did a great job. It is quite hard to judge from the outside...sitting in the dressing room, after the second day, if the wicketkeeper is standing up to a bowler who is two metres tall, that is worrying," Morkel said."Anshul gave us control. Let's support the guy as he bowls hard overs for the team.""The wicket lost a lot of pace early and hence the drop in pace of the bowlers. Wickets can get flat but you don't want them to lose pace ," he explained.With questions over India's pace-bowling resources and workload, Morkel said all the fast bowlers were fit and available, with the team set to make a selection call on the eve of the Test."All bowlers are fit and available and we will take a call tomorrow," he said.Morkel also addressed Mohammed Siraj's omission from the first Test, saying the senior pacer needed to assess his game and identify areas for improvement."Siraj is bowling well. Sometimes decisions are tough ones. My conversation with him was, 'Listen, let's step back a little and see where we can improve.' Selection, we can't control," Morkel said.The bowling coach said India needed to look beyond individual sessions and remain focused on the bigger objective of qualifying for the World Test Championship final."All these guys want to play the WTC final. After every bad session, we can't just get caught up. We have to break it down session by session and play our best brand of cricket," he said.Morkel also said Gurnoor Brar was pushing for a place in the team but needed to remain ready for when an opportunity came his way."Gurnoor is knocking on the door, doing all the right things. He has pace, bounce and will be ideal for these conditions. He just needs to be ready as and when he gets the opportunity. My job is to keep him 100 per cent ready," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd Test: Mohammed Siraj, Akash Deep or Gurnoor Brar? Team India face selection dilemma ahead of Christchurch Test
articles.summary: At around 6.33am India time on Tuesday, three days before the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, came a terse 13-word
articles.body: At around 6.33am India time on Tuesday, three days before the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, came a terse 13-word WhatsApp alert from the BCCI media team: “Nov 25, 2026 - Christchurch. India. No practice and no press conference. Thank you.”It was hardly unexpected. With just a three-day turnaround between the two Tests, including a travel day, India were never going to exert themselves immediately after sending down a combined 241 overs across New Zealand’s two innings at the Basin Reserve. The training blocks and practice games are behind them. India will have just one training session, on Thursday, before the second Test, and it is now all about recovery, selection and execution.India went into the Basin Test with four seamers, Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep, Prasidh Krishna and Anshul Kamboj, and every one of them put in a significant shift, often having to operate into Wellington’s unforgiving wind. Bumrah sent down 49 overs, Kamboj and Prasidh 45 each and Akash 43.After Monday’s dispiriting draw in a Test they had controlled for long periods, skipper Shubman Gill hinted that India may not tinker too much with their XI or, more pertinently, the combination.There is certainly little in Hagley’s history to encourage them to move away from a paceheavy attack. In the 15 men’s Tests played at the venue, 444 of the 484 wickets have gone to pacers. That’s a massive 91.7%.So four quicks again? Certainly. But will they be the same four?India’s batters appear to be in decent touch, with several of them also having had useful time in the middle here during the India ‘A’ game. It is the bowling attack where the more intriguing calls lie.Could the team management be tempted to hand the nippy Gurnoor Brar a Test debut in place of Anshul Kamboj? Kamboj had a decent outing with bat and ball at the Basin, but when the ball became older and New Zealand’s batters dug in, he appeared a little short of the variations required to keep prising out wickets.Brar, meanwhile, wasn’t part of the original Test squad. But after being adjudged Player of the Series in the ODIs, he was added to the Test party in place of leftarm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav.Can India turn back to the experience and inexhaustible energy of Mohammed Siraj in place of Akash Deep? That relentless intensity was something India missed at the Basin once the pitch flattened.The current regime under Gill and coach Gautam Gambhir has prioritised current form and the eye test in the nets. By the looks of it, Siraj hasn’t quite passed that test yet, despite Gill speaking glowingly about him in Wellington.But if Gill and Gambhir care for history, someone could perhaps point them towards one striking statistic. India have won nine Tests in SENA countries since 2020 and Siraj has featured in every one of them, playing significant roles along the way.Hagley, like the Basin, has a reputation for rewarding seam, with its grass cover offering the quicks assistance over the first couple of days before batting tends to become easier, particularly under bright skies. The forecast suggests sunshine over the first three days, but considerably more cloud and rain on Days Four and Five. That could make having fresh legs in the pace attack even more important.India were handed first use of the Basin pitch after winning the toss and reduced New Zealand to 70/5. At Hagley, should they win the toss again, expect them to have no hesitation in inserting New Zealand.History backs that instinct too: in the 15 Tests played here, teams winning the toss and choosing to bowl first have gone on to win nine times.With valuable World Test Championship points available before New Zealand head across the Tasman to face Australia and India prepare to host Australia for five Tests, both teams will desperately want a result.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Everyone who gave me grief': Ben Stokes' cheeky take on Shubman Gill ending 1st IND vs NZ Test early evokes Manchester memories
articles.summary: Ben Stokes took a cheeky swipe at his critics after Shubman Gill's decision to end the first India vs New Zealand Test early brought back memories of Manches...
articles.body:
Ben Stokes revisited the Manchester handshake controversy after the first India vs New Zealand Test ended early.

He noted Shubman Gill's concern over Daryl Mitchell being on 49 before the batter initiated the handshake.

The former England captain cheekily hit back at critics of his own early handshake against India in 2025.

What did Ben Stokes say about Shubman Gill's handshake against New Zealand?

India vs New Zealand Test match in Wellington saw an early draw, reminding people of the 2025 Manchester Test, where Ben Stokes was criticised by many for handing India an early handshake.

A post on Instagram regarding the current situation indicated that Ben would be happy with how things went down.

"Really like how Gill actually thought Mitchell is on 49 and might not shake hands but Mitchell just came forward himself. Ben Stokes would be happy," the post said.

Discussing the issue in an episode of That's Not Cricket , Ben explained that Gill seemed afraid that Mitchell wouldn't shake hands while scoring 49 runs and then stepped forward of his own accord, ending the game at 239/5.

"There was a lot of debate around that and I think this is now in front of me because what's happened is Shubman Gill of the Indian cricket team are in a position that we were as a team there in a result that was going to be a draw."

He continued, "And he was hoping that the opposition would shake hands so he could get his team off the field. But he thinks that someone being on 49, close to a landmark, means that they are not going to."

"Can we just say that everyone who reacted gave me a little grief. Can we get a reaction to Shubman Gill shaking hands and Daryl Mitchell doing the right thing by shaking hands when there cannot be a result? Thanks, Daryl."

What happened during the first India vs New Zealand Test in Wellington?

India and New Zealand shared an interesting draw in the first Test match held at the Basin Reserve, Wellington.

India had got themselves into a dominant position after declaring at 720/9. However, the gritty performance from the New Zealand batters ensured that India did not get anything out of the match.

New Zealand ended up at 239/5 with Daryl Mitchell being not out for 49 and Glenn Phillips at 26 when the decision to conclude the match was taken.

Gill's decision to shake hands with the opposition came while around 15 overs were still left in the day. The skipper explained his move by saying that his fast bowlers would be getting a lot of workload.

Why did Ben Stokes face criticism during the 2025 Manchester Test?

This was reminiscent of the fourth England against India Test at Old Trafford played in July 2025, where Stokes extended an early handshake with 15 overs left in the game.

But Ravindra Jadeja and Washington Sundar did not extend their hands in reciprocation, as they approached the century mark in their respective innings, scoring 89 runs and 80 runs respectively.

The two put on an unbeaten stand of 203 runs before declaring the innings at 425/4. It turned out to be a draw for the match.

The gesture of the England skipper led to heated arguments as to whether he was right in calling off the match even though there were personal goals to be scored by the opposition team members.

The Cricket News Opinion: Stokes gets his moment of vindication

Stokes' action can be forgiven considering the criticism he got after the Manchester Test. He was in the same predicament but with no hope of a result, whereas the Indian team decided to keep on batting.

The incident in Wellington provided a funny comparison. It seemed like Gill thought about whether Mitchell was ready to complete his half-century before making his move, but Mitchell came forward to shake hands.

Neither Gill nor Mitchell can be blamed because the captains have to think about the match situation as well as the chances of getting a result when deciding to end the game.

Nevertheless, Stokes was glad that he could make a comparison between their actions because he was criticised for his offer in Manchester.

articles.title: IPL 2027 mini-auction: Remaining purse and budget for each Indian Premier League team detailed
articles.summary: Check the remaining purse and auction budget for all 10 teams ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction in Goa, including the ₹157 crore salary cap and trade impact...
articles.body:
Franchises have swapped several big names in recent months.

One blockbuster exchange involving Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh stands out among the deals.

Purse sizes differ sharply across the ten teams before the mini-auction.

IPL 2027 auction purse remaining: Team-by-team budget breakdown after retention lists and deadline-day trades

With the IPL 2027 mini-auction on the horizon, every franchise is keeping a close watch on how much money it has left to spend.

Over the last few months, a good number of players have moved between teams through trades, many of them seeking a better role or more game time at their new teams. Some of these deals were straight swaps, while one was completed as a cash transaction.

The biggest name to change hands is Hardik Pandya, who has gone from Mumbai Indians to Punjab Kings for Rs 18 crore. Arshdeep Singh has travelled in the opposite direction at the same price, which means the two sides have effectively exchanged one star for another.

Rishabh Pant's return to Delhi Capitals for Rs 15 crore, with Kuldeep Yadav heading to Lucknow Super Giants at Rs 13.50 crore, is another marquee trade deal.

Harshal Patel's move from Sunrisers to Gujarat Titans for Rs 4 crore was the only cash deal on the list, and Rajasthan Royals added Mohammed Shami and Manimaran Siddharth from Lucknow in return for Sam Curran.

Retention list: CSK | MI | RCB | KKR | RR | SRH | PBKS | DC | LSG | GT

IPL 2027 auction purse details for all teams

How is the purse amount determined for each team?

Every franchise had the original purse of 120 crore ahead of last year's mega auction, through which they built their roster for the 2025-27 cycle.

Before each mini-auction, INR 5 crore is added to the purse, so teams in Goa on December 16 will be operating with a maximum of IR 130 crore (includes salary for retained players as well).

The IPL 2027 mini-auction will take place on Wednesday, December 16, 2026, in Goa, India.

The 10 franchises will have an opportunity to strengthen their squads by signing players from the auction pool.

The auction follows the November 17 retention deadline, when franchises submitted their final lists of retained and released players to the BCCI ahead of the event.

Meanwhile, the trade deadline continues until a week before the auction (December 9).

articles.title: 'Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting': World Cup-winner sends strong message on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances. But his stunning innings against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars could well be the most special of them all. The youngster went after the bowlers from the start and completely dominated the opposition attack.Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus.Many former cricketers and experts have backed the youngster for a regular place in India's T20I team. However, his latest knock also underlined his ability to make an impact in the 50-over format.Former India captain and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth feels the team management must take bold decisions to give Sooryavanshi a bigger role in Indian cricket.Srikkanth questions Gambhir's approachSooryavanshi has featured in 10 T20Is for India but is yet to cement his place in the playing XI. With the full-strength team available, Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been preferred as openers.Srikkanth feels the youngster is not getting enough opportunities despite his impressive performances. He also had a strong message for India head coach Gautam Gambhir."We need to make some strong moves. Vaibhav was made Bihar captain right away. He was the vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy; him and Ishan (Kishan) won the title. He has been promoted to that level. Gautam is just keeping deaf ears," Srikkanth said, speaking on his YouTube channel."The team management is playing one game, saying he has to be groomed, and not giving him chances. This guy, on the other hand, is playing his own game. You say it is not in your hands and all of that. Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting. No one can hit like this. Just look at this," he added.'This is another level'Srikkanth was left stunned by the variety of shots Sooryavanshi played during his remarkable innings. He also praised the youngster's power and timing, saying he had rarely seen anything like it."What is this? Have you seen anyone hitting the ball like this? Look at the shots he has played. He has his shots everywhere in all ranges. This is another level. This does not happen in book cricket either. I have never seen these kinds of shots. Who is this guy? Which generation is he from? Where does he get so much power and sense of timing?" he further said.Srikkanth also compared the 15-year-old's batting to that of some of the biggest hitters in the game, including AB de Villiers and Chris Gayle."I have not seen anyone playing like this in a team. Even (AB) De Villiers and (Chris) Gayle did not play like this," Srikkanth concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
